name: California

agency.name: California Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM), Department of Conservation

form.name: Notice of Intention (NOI) to drill, rework or abandon a well, filed online in WellSTAR (XML electronic data delivery template also accepted)
form.number: WellSTAR online form 'Notice of Intention'; EDD instructions EICD008 v3.13 (Release 5.0, 4/30/2020; template updated 07-23-20)
form.notes: The online form needs a WellSTAR operator login, so the cells come from two agency documents read in full: the NOI instructions for the XML electronic template (field-by-field list, 580 KB, HTTP 200, same size on a fresh HEAD) and the 'Submit NOI' user reference guide (15 steps; screenshots not readable as text). The forms page (HTTP 200) lists 28 WellSTAR forms; the NOI is 'apply for a permit to drill/rework or abandon a well' and is filed before drilling with a general plan showing location and total depth. Notice types: New Drill, Deepen, Sidetrack, Rework, Abandon, Re-Abandon, with a supplementary-notice flag. Steps: organization and notice type; XML upload option; operator contacts; well information (proposed well type, bond, lease, mineral and surface ownership, well name and number, field, area, pool, flags for exploratory, dry hole, confidentiality, well stimulation, H2S, UIC or gas storage project, thermal recovery); depth datum, elevation, MD and TVD, direction, fresh water and USDW zones, geologic markers, BOP and drilling program (mud system, disposal); surface and bottom-hole locations; casing and cement; completion intervals and perforations; proposed work; CEQA; document upload; directional survey. The permit is the NOI approval. A 2024 notice to operators says a permit lapses if work does not start within 24 months. The form was not compared with a live screen, so a newer field may exist.

api_number.n: API in the Notices layer and the weekly lists; CalGEM assigns it, so a new-drill row already carries one

well_name.n: WellDesignation, LeaseName, WellNumber; the NOI asks well number and well name

lease_name.n: LeaseName in the layer 1 schema (blanks not checked); the NOI links a lease record

operator_name.n: OperatorName in layer 1; Operator Name in the weekly lists

operator_id.n: OperatorCode (integer) in layer 1; operator is picked from an Organization list on the NOI

operator_type.n: Organizational Questionnaire form not read; the NOI has no such item

bond.n: NOI step 4: link an existing or newly submitted bond; not in the permit layers

county.n: County in layer 1 (CountyName in the Wells layer); not in the weekly lists

district.n: District in layer 1 and the weekly lists (Northern, Central, Southern)

field_pool.n: FieldName, AreaName in layer 1; the NOI also asks the pool(s)

surface_latlon.n: Latitude, Longitude (NAD83) in layer 1; entered by the operator on the NOI

surface_plss.n: Section, Township, Range, BaseMeridian in layer 1; no footages (NOI asks a corner call)

bottom_hole_loc.n: NOI asks proposed bottom-hole section, township, range, lat/lon, county, corner call; not in layer

lateral_path.n: NOI steps 12-13: directional survey (XML template or online); required for directional/horizontal

elevation.n: Proposed elevation of ground above sea level (required) and depth datum height above ground

surface_owner.n: NOI asks if mineral and surface ownership coincide and the surface owner category (Federal etc.)

well_type.n: WellType code and WellTypeLabel (Oil & Gas, Cyclic Steam, Water Disposal...); NOI 'Proposed Well Type'

work_type.n: NoticeType: NOI - New Drill, Rework, Sidetrack, Deepen, Abandon, Re-Abandon

well_direction.n: Wells layer isDirectionallyDrilled Y/N (wells only, no horizontal split); NOI asks the direction

proposed_depth_md.n: Proposed bottom-hole depth (MD), optional field on the NOI

proposed_depth_tvd.n: Proposed bottom-hole depth (TVD), optional field on the NOI

lateral_length.n: No lateral-length item in the NOI field list; could be derived from the directional survey

target_formation.n: NOI asks pool(s), intended completion zones and interval formation; layer 1 has field and area only

formation_tops.n: Zones of Significance (fresh water, USDW, markers) with top/bottom TVD and MD, plus a markers text

casing_program.n: Wellbore features: type, top and bottom MD, outside and inside diameter, weight, grade, new or pulled

cement_program.n: Cement segments (top, bottom, inside or outside casing), cement class, volume, yield

pressure_control.n: BOP equipment: annular, pipe, blind and shear rams, rotating head, with pressure ratings

h2s.n: H2S anticipated checkbox and concentration; a contingency plan must be uploaded if checked

pit_waste.n: Mud system, mud disposal method, cuttings disposal; salt formations, oil or salt-based fluids

water.n: Asks only whether fresh water or a USDW is present; no water source or volume item in the field list

fracture_plan.n: Only a checkbox that the NOI accompanies a well stimulation permit request; the plan is on the WST form

frac_dates.n: Disclosure form asks each stage's start and end; state law makes the public registry searchable by time period

frac_chemicals.n: Form asks chemical name and CAS; state law makes the public registry searchable by both; open map layers hold none

frac_additives.n: Form asks trade name, supplier and purpose; registry searchable by additive; open map layers hold none

frac_amounts.n: Form asks percent by mass per chemical; state law puts it in the public registry; open map layers hold none

spacing_unit.n: No spacing, acreage or pooling item in the NOI field list

spacing_exception.n: No exception request; critical-well and sensitive-area flags with a distance text only

mineral_owner.n: Mineral owner category on the lease step (Federal if BLM land); lease record linked

fee.n: No fee item in the NOI guide or field list; fee schedule not read

notice_hearing.n: CEQA step only: lead agency, local agency contact, CEQA document and notice type; no offset-owner notice

date_approved.n: NoticeDateDetermination (layer 1), Date Determination (weekly list); epoch ms in UTC

date_expires.n: WellSTAR tracks it (24 months after the NOI, per a 2024 notice) but no file or page showing it was seen

spud_date.n: SpudDate in the Wells layer (text MM/DD/YYYY); sparse for new wells; not on the permit rows

completion_date.n: Well Summary is a separate form; no completion column in the Wells or permit layers

status.n: NoticeStatus (Approved, Closed, Canceled, Submitted); WellStatus in the Wells layer

plat_image.n: Forms page: NOI is filed with a general plan showing proposed location and total depth; Maps is an upload type

form_image.n: Public well records are online (entry page needs a disclaimer click) but contents not checked

completion_report.n: Well Summary form not read; not checked whether public records show it

production_link.n: Agency page lists production and injection summary reports (SQL Server .BAK); not opened

sources.tested: Fresh query 2026-11-01: layer 1 count where NoticeType = 'NOI - New Drill' returned HTTP 200 {"count":472}. Earlier fetches (2026-10-31): service folder, layer schema (maxRecordCount 2000; JSON, GeoJSON, PBF; Query capability), a statistics query by NoticeType and NoticeStatus: Approved 7,350 (Abandon 5,185; Rework 1,076; Sidetrack 498; New Drill 452; Re-Abandon 131; Deepen 8), Closed 1,118, Canceled 51: 8,519 rows in all. Earliest NoticeDateDetermination 2024-11-01, latest 2026-10-31 (current to the day), so the layer looks like a rolling window of about 24 months (not verified). New Drill by determination month: 2025 had 8 in all, 2026 has 464 in the layer (Jan 31, Feb 52, Mar 109, Apr 107, May 33, Jun 13, Jul 36, Aug 27, Sep 19, Oct 37; the year-to-date workbook counts 471 through Oct 24). Dates are epoch milliseconds (UTC). No supplementary-permit flag in the layer.

grade_reason: The Notices map service (layer 1) is free, needs no login, answered HTTP 200 today, has one row per approved notice or permit with a determination (approval) date, a work-type column (NoticeType) and a well-type column, and is current to the day. Limits: the layer begins in November 2024 (about 24 months), and older weeks are only by file request.
producer_plan: Source: layer 1 of the WellSTAR Notices service, queried with where=1=1, outFields=NoticeType,NoticeStatus,NoticeDateDetermination,WellTypeLabel,County,OperatorCode,API, returnGeometry=false, in pages of 2,000 using resultOffset (about 8,500 rows, five requests, a pause between each; a full rebuild takes under a minute). Convert NoticeDateDetermination from epoch milliseconds to a California (Pacific) calendar date before counting months, because an approval at 00:12 UTC is the evening before. Keep NoticeStatus Approved and Closed (Closed means the work was reported); decide separately on Canceled (51 rows: approved and later canceled or withdrawn; the layer does not say which). Bands: new = NOI - New Drill; reentry = Rework, Sidetrack, Deepen (Rework covers all re-entry for secondary work, including recompletions and conversions, so recomplete cannot be split out); injection = any of these on a well whose WellType is an injector (Water Disposal, Waterflood, Steamflood, Injection, Air Injection, Gas Disposal, Pressure Maintenance; Cyclic Steam wells are producers); other = Abandon and Re-Abandon (plugging, about 70 percent of rows). Amendments: the layer has no supplementary flag; only the 2026 weekly workbooks do (31 of 2,813 permits), so amend counts would need those files and cover 2026 only. History: months before 2024-11 are not in the layer; the weekly workbooks (2026 on the page) and file-request archives (older) would be needed. Caveats: New Drill permits were almost absent in 2025 (8 in the layer) and surged in 2026 (about 465), so a trend line is dominated by policy, not demand; spud dates (Wells layer, text field) are sparse and late, so use permits, not spuds. For a freshness check, compare the layer's newest determination date with the latest weekly report.
privacy_notes: The permit layers and weekly lists carry operator organization names, an operator code, well names, API numbers and well coordinates; no contact names, phone numbers or e-mails were seen in them (checked column names and sample rows). The NOI itself collects contact name, phone and e-mail for the filing, but these are not published. Some small operators may be individuals; names were not screened.
